nice_guideline_used: NG136 (Hypertension), CG181/PH46 (CVD risk), NG28 (Prediabetes), NICE anaemia guidance

medications.purpose: Control blood pressure and provide renal protection
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line therapy for essential hypertension

medications.purpose: Add diuretic component; preferred over HCTZ in metabolic syndrome
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 advises indapamide as the preferred thiazide‑like diuretic in triple therapy

medications.dose: 5 mg once daily (increase to 10 mg if BP target not met)
medications.purpose: Second antihypertensive agent to achieve <140/90 mmHg
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 step 2 recommends ACE‑I + CCB when monotherapy insufficient

medications.purpose: Primary‑prevention of cardiovascular disease in metabolic‑syndrome
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181/PH46: statin indicated when QRISK ≥10 % or ≥2 metabolic‑syndrome components

medications.dose: Start 500 mg once daily, titrate to 500 mg twice daily over 2 weeks
medications.duration: Lifelong – review HbA1c every 3 months; discontinue if eGFR falls <30 mL/min/1.73 m²
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 recommends metformin for high‑risk pre‑diabetes when lifestyle alone insufficient

medications.dose: 200 mg (≈65 mg elemental iron) three times daily with meals
medications.duration: 8 weeks, then reassess Hb and ferritin; continue if still deficient
medications.nice_justification: Standard therapy for iron‑deficiency anaemia (NICE anaemia guidance)

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive potassium retention and possible reduction in renal function
interactions_checked.action: Check serum potassium and eGFR 1–2 weeks after change, then annually

interactions_checked.interaction: Synergistic blood‑pressure lowering; risk of symptomatic hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Start amlodipine at 5 mg, monitor BP and symptoms during first 2 weeks

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine can increase atorvastatin plasma levels modestly (CYP3A4 interaction)
interactions_checked.action: Use lowest effective statin dose; advise patient to report muscle pain; consider CK if symptomatic

interactions_checked.interaction: Iron may reduce absorption of other oral drugs
interactions_checked.action: Take iron at least 2 hours apart from other medications

contraindications.reason: Risk of lactic acidosis if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²
contraindications.alternative: If eGFR 30‑45, start 500 mg daily with careful monitoring; if <30, consider DPP‑4 inhibitor

contraindications.reason: Worsens glucose tolerance and lipid profile in metabolic syndrome
May worsen glucose tolerance and mask hypoglycaemia; not indicated per NICE NG136
contraindications.alternative: Calcium channel blocker (amlodipine) added to ACE‑I

assumptions_warnings: eGFR/serum creatinine not available – assumed ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m² for ACE‑I, metformin, indapamide safety.
Serum potassium not available – assumed ≤4.5 mmol/L.
HbA1c / fasting glucose not available – assumed pre‑diabetes; metformin initiation pending confirmation.
Lipid profile not available – assumed elevated LDL; statin initiation pending confirmation.
Liver function tests not available – assumed normal for statin safety.
Iron studies (ferritin, transferrin saturation) not available – ferrous sulphate pending confirmation of iron‑deficiency.
QRISK score not calculated – assumed ≥10 % based on hypertension, obesity, pre‑diabetes; statin justified per metabolic‑syndrome criteria.
Blood pressure readings not provided – assumed ≥140/90 mmHg despite current therapy.
treatment_summary: Continue lisinopril, replace hydrochlorothiazide with indapamide SR, add amlodipine 5 mg daily and atorvastatin 20 mg nightly to achieve blood‑pressure and cardiovascular‑risk targets. Start metformin MR 500 mg daily (titrate to BID) and ferrous sulphate 200 mg TDS after confirming renal function, glucose status, and iron deficiency respectively. Monitor BP, electrolytes, renal function, HbA1c, lipid profile, and iron studies as outlined; review medications annually.
